newsitem.title: HONG KONG: High costs drive HK jewellery producers to China.
newsitem.headline: High costs drive HK jewellery producers to China.

text.p: Hong Kong jewellery makers are moving more production to China to take advantage of cheaper labour and land, leaving Hong Kong to evolve into a centre for design and management, an industry spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Our difficulty comes mainly from the high cost of labour and land, which is why I see Hong Kong moving towards a management type situation, while the production will be more and more on the China side," said Karl Shin, chairman of Hong Kong's Jewellery Manufacturers' Association.
Shin was speaking after a news conference at the 14th Hong Kong International Jewellery Show being held in the British colony from Wednesday to Saturday.

About a quarter of Hong Kong's total jewellery exports were fabricated in China, Shin estimated. In 1996, Hong Kong exported HK$10.6 billion ($1.3 billion) worth of jewellery, of which about 38 percent went to the United States.

Hong Kong companies underwrite factories in China because only Chinese companies have the right to produce jewellery in the country, said Shin, who also is managing director of K K Jewellery Co Ltd, which designs, manufactures and exports jewellery.
The Hong Kong companies supply funds, production facilities, techonology and management, he said.
Hong Kong jewellery makers could export gold to China under conditions tightly controlled by the People's Bank of China (PBOC), the country's central bank, and by customs.
After production, similarly tight procedures controlled jewellery exports from China, Shin said.

With the recent drop in gold prices, people were buying more gold, particularly 24 carat gold jewellery, Shin said. Local market demand had increased about 25 percent to 30 percent from the beginning of last year, he noted.

This year was expected to be a bonanza for the jewellery sector in Hong Kong as the economy picked up and tourists poured in to witness the colony's return to Chinese sovereignty June 30,1997, Shin said.
Last year, visitors to Hong Kong bought jewellery worth about HK$7.9 billion, up 14 percent over 1995.
